comment: Photographs the scenario harness may measure against, fetched on demand into a cache outside every repository and never committed. This manifest is the citable artefact: it records where each image comes from, the exact bytes expected, the licence, and what characteristic it is there to exercise. Every download is checked against its digest before use, and a mismatch is treated exactly like a missing file - the run falls back to generated content and says so, because an image that changed silently would change the measurements silently. Adding an image is a data change: only works whose licence permits redistribution and modification with no attribution carried in the file belong here.
licence_note: All of these are works of the United States federal government, in the public domain by 17 U.S.C. 105. No attribution is required; the credits below are a courtesy. Right of publicity is separate from copyright, so a face here must never be repurposed into anything implying that the person shown endorses this software. That is why face-portrait.jpg - a living astronaut's official portrait - is test tooling only and is kept out of the public demo, while skin-and-colour.jpg may appear there: it is a 1942 archival photograph, and nothing about it invites the reading that its subject endorses software made eighty years later.

images.name: face-portrait.jpg
images.purpose: a real face for the face-lock path, and skin tones for the vectorscope's skin line

images.name: skin-and-colour.jpg
images.purpose: skin tones beside a strongly saturated red and a large near-neutral field, which is the whole vectorscope lesson in one frame - the skin line, an excursion to the graticule, and a centre to read them against
images.credit: Library of Congress / Alfred T. Palmer, Office of War Information, October 1942

images.name: saturated-colour.jpg
images.purpose: strongly saturated varied colour, which pushes the vectorscope out towards its graticule
images.credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service / Dave Menke

images.name: neutral-detail.jpg
images.purpose: near-neutral areas with fine high-frequency detail, the expensive case for every engine
images.credit: Yellowstone National Park / National Park Service

images.name: flat-field.jpg
images.purpose: a mostly uniform field, the cheap case, where a change detector should find almost nothing
images.credit: Yellowstone National Park / National Park Service

images.name: wide-tonal-range.jpg
images.purpose: deep shadow beside clipped highlight, which fills the waveform and the histogram end to end
